quizName: DMV Practice Test #11 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: To improve your chances of being seen, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or when visibility is poor.
Always use your headlight.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use your headlight.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to keep your headlight on at all times.

questions.question: When motorcyclists ride in a group:

options.text: Inexperienced riders should lead the group.
Inexperienced riders should be near the front of the group.
Inexperienced riders should be in the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Inexperienced riders should be near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, behind the leader. This allows experienced riders to lead and watch the less experienced riders.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn
No left turn
No U-turn

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This is a traffic sign with red and black markings. It means U-turns are not allowed in this area.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You will have time to react to hazards.
You will have space to maneuver.
You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will have more time to accelerate when entering a curve.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time to react and room to maneuver if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
Be able to keep both hands on the handle grips during the turn.
Prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before turning. Shifting gears during a turn can cause a sudden power change to the rear wheel, which may cause skidding.

questions.question: Grabbing the front brake or slamming the rear brake:

options.text: Can cause the brakes to lock.
Is the best way to stop in an emergency.
Is the best way to slow down when the streets are wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause the brakes to lock.
questions.explanation: Grabbing the front brake or slamming the rear brake can lock the brakes. This can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: Your motorcycle should fit you properly, meaning:

options.text: Your fingertips should barely reach the handlebars when seated.
The seat should be one foot higher than your waist when standing next to it.
Your feet should comfortably touch the ground when seated.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your feet should comfortably touch the ground when seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly if your feet can comfortably touch the ground while you are seated. Make sure the motorcycle fits before you ride.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, your feet should be:

options.text: On the footrests for balance.
Pointed with your toes aiming downward.
Relaxed.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the footrests for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. Do not point your toes downward, as they may get caught between the road and the footrests.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean you cannot pass. Dashed white lines mean you may pass if it is safe.

questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, your arms should:

options.text: Have a large bend at the elbow when reaching for the handlebars.
Be slightly bent when holding the handlebars.
Be fully extended when reaching for the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be slightly bent when holding the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Your arms should have a slight bend when holding the handlebars. This reduces arm fatigue and lets you press on the handlebars without stretching.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Avoid sudden moves because they can cause a skid.
Ride on the shoulder to stay away from traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake does not work on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves because they can cause a skid.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, any sudden change in speed or direction can cause a skid. Be smooth and gentle when you speed up, shift gears, turn, or brake.

questions.question: Blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Are nothing to worry about.
Should be checked regularly by riders.
Do not exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked regularly by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots just like other vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your normal riding routine.

questions.question: Increase your following distance if:

options.text: It is raining.
There is light traffic.
It is sunny.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is raining.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when it takes longer to stop, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and other vehicles may cut in front of you.

questions.question: Alcohol reaches the brain ________ being consumed.

options.text: Within minutes of
About an hour after
About two hours after

questions.correctAnswerText: Within minutes of
questions.explanation: Alcohol reaches the brain and affects your riding ability within minutes of drinking. Riding while under the influence is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If you are being passed, you should:

options.text: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding too close to the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding too far away may cause the driver to return to your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: Where should you position your motorcycle when entering a curve?

options.text: The outside of the curve
The inside of the curve
Wherever traffic and road conditions require

questions.correctAnswerText: Wherever traffic and road conditions require
questions.explanation: Every curve is different. Choose a lane position that fits the conditions and adjust as needed.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks up while stopping on a surface with good traction, you should:

options.text: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake and then quickly re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the wheel locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: If the rear wheel locks while stopping on good traction, you can keep it locked until you stop. You can control your motorcycle even with a locked rear wheel if it stays upright and travels straight.

questions.question: When being passed, moving to the part of your lane that is farthest from the passing vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be farther from the passing vehicle.
Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.
Is not encouraged or discouraged because it has no impact on safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because it may cause the other driver to return to your lane too soon.
questions.explanation: Do not move to the far part of your lane when being passed. This may encourage the passing driver to move back into your lane before it is safe.

questions.question: You are most likely to get into a collision:

options.text: At an intersection.
When riding in a group.
While traveling on the expressway.

questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection.
questions.explanation: Intersections have the greatest risk for conflicts between you and other traffic.

questions.question: Stopping in a turn is difficult because:

options.text: There is less traction available for stopping when the bike is leaning.
The rider is usually focused on the turn and not on braking.
The brake controls do not work in turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is less traction available for stopping when the bike is leaning.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. Some traction is used to make the turn while leaning, so less traction is available for stopping.

questions.question: Which lane position makes a motorcyclist most visible to other drivers?

options.text: The right
The center
The left

questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: When traffic allows, ride in the center of the lane. This position puts you in the driver's rearview mirror behind you. Be ready to change positions if traffic or road conditions require it.

questions.question: Which surface may give poor traction to a motorcycle?

options.text: Pavement markings
Dry pavement
The roadway under a bridge

questions.correctAnswerText: Pavement markings
questions.explanation: Poor traction can happen on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement. It can also happen on gravel roads, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: Your body removes the alcohol faster.
The alcohol builds up in your body faster.
The alcohol affects your body less.

questions.correctAnswerText: The alcohol builds up in your body faster.
questions.explanation: When you drink quickly, alcohol builds up in your body faster. Your body removes alcohol at a rate of about one drink per hour. If you drink more than one drink in an hour, alcohol will still be in your system after one hour.

questions.question: Which is NOT an important factor when choosing riding clothes?

options.text: The clothing protects you from heat and cold.
The clothing makes you more visible to others.
The clothing does not create unusual tan lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: The clothing does not create unusual tan lines.
questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you from injury in a crash. They also help prevent crashes by making you more visible. They protect you from discomforts like heat, cold, road debris, and hot or moving parts of the motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slippery when wet
Lanes shift
Yield

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols or words. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.
